findings.title: Default datetime evaluated once at class definition time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass default evaluated once when the module is loaded, not per-instance. All AssignmentSource instances created without explicitly passing `queued` will share the same stale timestamp (the time the module was imported), not the time the instance was created. This should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: where_should_sync does not pass sync_source to should_sync
findings.body: In `where_should_sync`, `installation.should_sync(key)` is called without a `sync_source` argument, so this path never benefits from the new assignment-source cycle-breaking logic. If this function is used anywhere relevant to assignment sync, cycles could still occur through this code path.

findings.title: Sync-cycle check compares integration_id to org_integration.integration_id but AssignmentSource is built from models.Integration without currently-synced-integration disambiguation
findings.body: `should_sync` only guards against the same integration that originated the change; it does not persist/propagate the assignment_source through intermediate inbound sync tasks (e.g. `sync_status_inbound`), so chains of different sync types between the same integration are not fully protected, and other call sites (e.g. status sync inbound task) are not shown to pass assignment_source consistently, risking partial fixes for the described loop.
